title: Never Miss a Customer Call Again (AI Receptionist)
lesson: Repeated customer questions and unanswered calls consume attention; the useful product story should show a relevant inquiry becoming an answer, booking or handoff, then explain the human benefit.
opening: An unanswered-call scenario is paired with a negative colour cue, then a competitor consequence. This gives the viewer a recognisable business cost before the personal event example.
story_arc: Missed call → competitor risk → personal virtual event → underestimated question volume → impatient customers → receptionist introduction → question/answer and channel examples → booking/FAQ/routing claims → busy-team fallback → language claim → worried-versus-focused owner contrast → branded trial CTA.
payoff: The short makes the workload and desired benefit concrete and shows several recognisable interface examples. It does not prove the numerical booking count, automatic answering, multilingual fluency or customer outcomes; some example screens do not match the current spoken claim.
selection_reason: A dense full-length mix of human problem scenes, split product orientation, progressive question cards, one local avatar selection, a targeted call-control pointer, numeric emphasis, short demonstrations and a human outcome contrast. It distinguishes new pictures from actual action/result evidence.
review_limits: All six chronological 2 fps context pages were inspected, plus avatar-selection and call-focus strips sampled every sixth decoded source frame and a full-resolution messaging frame. The strip manifests preserve frame indices and PTS from the native scan. Audio was not auditioned in this expansion. Spoken ideas come from timed caption sidecars checked against visible context; their timestamps contain anomalies and extend past the 55.933333-second visual rendition. Beat boundaries are approximate editorial partitions, not verified source edit points; exact-index strips refine only inspected intervals. No easing, response authenticity or unseen click result is claimed. These are source observations and proposed planning decisions, not a rendered replica or qualified template.
